data.narrative:
Inertia Enterprises is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Jeff Lawson, Annie Kritcher, and Mike Dunne that has raised $450M to date. The valuation landscape in Climate & Energy comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage peers in the narrow Climate & Energy universe. Using total capital raised ($450M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A progression to subsequent rounds, this method implies a valuation of $900M. Peer-median comparison was not viable; while nine same-sector companies exist, none met minimum thresholds (≥3 datapoints) for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filtering. A broad sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $765M to $1.0B, with a median of $900M. This estimate carries material uncertainty inherent in single-method triangulation and the absence of precise comparable transaction data at this stage and sector. Key risks to valuation include stage-progression multiplier assumptions and the early-stage liquidity profile of climate technology ventures.
